Occurrences.Kwic: 何不道？山擬開口，被師一橈打落水中。山纔上船，師又曰：道！道！山擬開口，師又打。山豁然大悟，乃點頭三下。師曰：竿頭絲線從君弄，不犯清波意自殊。由遂問：拋綸擲鈎，師意如何？師曰：絲懸綠水，浮定有無之意。山曰：語帶玄而無路，舌頭談而不談。師曰：釣盡江波，金鱗始遇。山乃掩耳。師曰：如是！如是！乃囑曰：汝向去直須藏身處沒蹤跡，沒蹤跡處莫藏身。吾二十年在藥山，祇明斯事。汝今既得，他後莫住城隍聚落，但向深山裡、钁頭邊，覔取一個半個接續，無令斷絕。山乃辭行，頻頻回顧。師遂喚：闍黎！山乃回首。師竪起橈子曰：汝將謂別有。乃覆船入水而逝。通容曰：夾山若不是道吾與他指引，於船子處決不能開發，故夾山悟道而道吾有功也。然夾山受船子囑付，尚復頻頻回顧，心猶未死
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X65/X65n1286.xml). Record of Tongs and Hammer in the Patriarchal Courtyard. Chuanzi Decheng owns the retained root: the charge — from now on you must hide where there is no trace, and in the traceless place do not hide. Twenty years I was at Yaoshan and understood only this matter; now that you have it, do not dwell in towns and gathering places — go into the deep mountains, to the mattock's edge, and find one or half a one to carry it on; do not let it break. Jiashan took leave and kept turning to look back; Chuanzi called: reverend! and as Jiashan turned his head, raised the oar: you thought there was something else — and overturned the boat, going into the water and gone. And Feiyin Tongrong's comment: had Jiashan not been pointed the way by Daowu, the boat would never have opened him — so in Jiashan's awakening Daowu shares the credit.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1405.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shixi Xinyue. Shixi Xinyue owns the retained address: hide where there is no trace; in the traceless place, do not hide. The man of old who spoke so never got out of the nest — and today, taking hands on Zhongshan, shoulder to shoulder in the imperial street — does speech like that get out of the nest or not? A long silence: slowly, slowly.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1360.xml). Expanded Record of Chan Master Xiatang Huiyuan. Xiatang Huiyuan owns the retained retelling: Chuanzi said — so it is, so it is — and charged him: from now on you must hide where there is no trace, and in the traceless place do not hide; twenty years I was at Yaoshan and understood only this; go into the deep mountains, to the mattock's edge, find one or half a one, continue the sage's life of wisdom, do not let it break. Jiashan took leave, kept turning back; Chuanzi called — reverend! reverend! — and as he turned, raised the oar: you thought there was something else — overturned the boat and was gone. And the verdict: here the great matter was still unlit — one agreeing phrase, a donkey-tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas, had already taken him alive; it is at Jiashan's nodding that he first reached home.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. Tianyin Yuanxiu owns the retained colophon: the monk Chuanzi, who had Yaoshan's seal, poled a little boat more than thirty years by the river, receiving those who came, none to his liking; when he met Jiashan he struck the poison blow — one oar knocked him into the great waves — make him speak with the hook three inches away: this is the claw and tooth of the founding teachers. And in that exchange he said — hide where there is no trace; in the traceless place, do not hide — which is exactly a dragon's head on a snake's tail; that is why when Jiashan later received Luopu, the brokenness was not little. And yet this is what mind sealing mind means, mind no different from mind — just watch the end, kicking the boat over: what a maneuver! Readers of his lines who take them as songs go to hell swift as an arrow; those who refuse them as songs go to hell just as fast. Leave both sides and produce one sentence — then I grant you have seen Chuanzi face to face.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB178.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Feiyin. Feiyin Tongrong owns the retained stupa verse: the filial disciples Feihuan and Benming, bringing their late teacher the elder Lianru's sacred bones into the stupa, asked the master to lift the bones — and he said: hide where there is no trace; in the traceless place, do not hide; dwelling in neither of the two, the scenery is fresh beyond measure — green bamboo and gray pears forever his companions, clear wind and bright moon admitted as neighbors; the one with eyes gets it for himself, and the ten-thousand-year flowing stream does not know spring. And he sent the bones in.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB466.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baishan Kai of Shanxi. Baishan Dekai owns the retained address: the man of old — I have a broken-legged pot; you, lift and carry it for me — then: then you and the master go out with the same one hand. Baishan: Longshan today — summon me the seat-leader and the rector. Someone: what does the master want with them? This mountain monk told him — I have a tortoise-hair whisk, to hold crosswise and use upside-down; and if someone said — then you and the master go out with the same one hand — I would tell him: the reverend has said me right. Asked further: and after that, what? — I answered: hide where there is no trace; in the traceless place, do not hide. And the whisk flung down: a golden pellet fresh from the red furnace, smashing through the reverend's iron face.

Senses.Explanation: Hide where there is no trace; in the traceless place, do not hide — the boatman's parting charge, sealed with an overturned boat and graded for a thousand years. At the root, Chuanzi Decheng charges Jiashan: from now on you must hide where there is no trace, and in the traceless place do not hide; twenty years I was at Yaoshan and understood only this — go into the deep mountains, to the mattock's edge, find one or half a one, do not let it break; and as Jiashan turned back once more, the oar rose — you thought there was something else — the boat overturned, and the boatman was gone; Feiyin Tongrong comments: without Daowu's pointing, the boat would never have opened him. Shixi Xinyue, opening the hall with the charge itself: the man of old who spoke so never got out of the nest — today, hands taken on Zhongshan, shoulders touching in the imperial street — does speech like that get out of the nest or not? slowly, slowly. Xiatang Huiyuan, retelling the scene and staking it: the great matter still unlit — one agreeing phrase, a donkey-tethering stake for ten thousand kalpas, had already taken him alive; it is at Jiashan's nodding that he first reached home. Tianyin Yuanxiu, inscribing the Chuanzi collection: thirty years a little boat by the river, none to his liking; then Jiashan — one oar into the great waves, speak with the hook three inches off; and in that exchange he said the charge — which is exactly a dragon's head on a snake's tail, hence the brokenness when Jiashan later received Luopu; and yet mind sealing mind, mind no different from mind — watch the boat kicked over: what a maneuver; song-readers go to hell like an arrow, song-refusers just as fast — leave both, and I grant you have seen Chuanzi. Feiyin Tongrong, lifting the bones of the elder Lianru into the stupa: hide where there is no trace; in the traceless place, do not hide; dwelling in neither of the two, the scenery fresh beyond measure — the ten-thousand-year flowing stream does not know spring. Baishan Dekai, asked what comes after: I have a tortoise-hair whisk, held crosswise, used upside-down; the reverend has said me right; and after that — hide where there is no trace; in the traceless place, do not hide; the whisk flung down: a golden pellet fresh from the red furnace, smashing through the reverend's iron face.
